utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today we are Wednesday, the 20th of February, 2008. I'd like to greet the representatives of the Prosecution, the witness, Mr. Seselj, as well as all the people assisting us in the courtroom. The examination-in-chief will resume today unless Mr. Seselj has something to tell us. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, a terrible problem has occurred, and as we're talking about a confidential decision, you know that in principle I am against any form of confidentiality, but I would nonetheless like to draw your attention so that perhaps you could issue the order to move to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am not in a position yet to inform Your Honours about progress regarding disclosure of certain documents that are subject to and requests for protective measures, so on that I cannot update you. There was also another issue of whether or not the Prosecution had the decree or the decision establishing an imminent -- the state of imminent threat of war, and indeed that exhibit which Mr. Seselj requested is 65 ter number 592 on the Prosecution exhibit list, and I have copies here that I can hand out, and in light of yesterday's discussions maybe it would be appropriate to admit these into evidence. I --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have to remind you, Mr. President, that you asked this of the Prosecution yesterday, principally you, and then that I help the Prosecutor by telling him where he could find it, but it was the Trial Chamber who actually asked for the document yesterday. I might have supported your request, but you requested it first. So the Prosecutor would have had to have come by that document himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever the case may be, what -- what matters is that we have the documents which was published in the Official Gazette on the 18th of October, 1991. So can we have an exhibit number, please. This is a well-known document. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another objection to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will recall that yesterday both the Prosecutor and the witness throughout said that the imminent threat of war was established on the 3rd of October, 1991, and as naive as I am, without having the documents in fronts of me I believed them, but you could see that it was the 1st of October, in fact, when an act on the proclamation of a state of war was proclaimed the day when we transformed the Crisis Staff into the War Staff of the Serbian Radical Party. So that's just what happened yesterday. So I was taken in by that trick of theirs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. True to fact the document does that it is the 1 of October not the 18th. Could we have an exhibit number and then the witness will be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... P220.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm sure that this would be an issue in cross-examination in due course. Your Honours, we left off yesterday at a point when we were going through various documents relative to the War Staff of the SRS, and if Your Honours would go to where we left off yesterday in binder 1, the next documents I would like to discuss with the witness begins with Exhibit number 65 ter 486. It's like three-fourths down in the binder. And the issue that I was going to bring up with the witness concerned the issue of reports received by the War Staff. President Judge Antonetti already raised this issue on the first day of the testimony of the witness, and the reference that is at pages 3656 and 3657 of the transcript, where he mentioned two specific reports, 65 ter number 459, and I apologise, maybe that is actually the exhibit we should begin with, which is -- if you found the document I just mentioned, it's just the document before what I just said. And the second document, the second report, is Exhibit number 486. Could we -- without displaying it to the public, could we call up 5 -- sorry, 459, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you mentioned this report the other day, but could you just remind us? What is this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is a report which was compiled by Zoran Rankic, the deputy chief of the SRS War Staff who addresses in the report his observations during the visit he carried out to Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and I would like to draw your attention to the first three lines of the document where the author says that he was sent by the order of the staff and the president Dr. Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, what is the date of this document? Do we have that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I don't believe we have a date on the document or at least it's difficult to read at least that's what the translation says I don't know if -- sometime in 1991 if Your Honour look at the bottom of the second page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding is it's the 2nd of September, 1991, Your Honours. Maybe see --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If you look at the B/C/S version on the last page, it says "Belgrade, 02 --" it looks like 09, 1991. And, Your Honours, if you've found the document in the binder, then if you would like to flip to the next document which is then 486, which may we also call up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are going very fast with this 4 -- first document 459. Now, Witness, a report has been prepared by Mr. Rankic following an order given by the staff and the president, Mr. Seselj. This person went to Slavonia to visit the units there who were seemingly on the ground, on the battleground. We don't know whether it was a battle ground or not, but anyway. So as you are a military expert, what can you conclude thereof? How are we to understand this? From your point of view, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it -- it supports the conclusion I drew earlier that the SRS War Staff is acting as a military staff organ whereby the Party Staff and the president Vojislav Seselj can issue orders to the SRS War Staff to visit volunteer units or SRS volunteer units on the field, whereby I think when we finish the whole sentence, the first sentence, Rankic doesn't only go to just visit the units as some kind of a social activity, but he also goes to relay so to forward an order to withdraw in order to re-group forces. So this indicates that the War Staff and Mr. Seselj are in a position to issue orders to their volunteers on the field.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down somewhat, Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. And the dates is it's sent on the 3rd of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now if we look at this in detail, he arrived on the 31st of August around 8.00 p.m. seeming think there is an operation going on. There are mortars, there is shelling. And he contacts the commander Branislav Gavrilovic and his deputy Miroslav Vukotic. So this unit has a commander. That commander is Gavrilovic. Who does he report to in military terms? Who does he report to, this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document does not allow to draw such a conclusion. What I do know from looking at other documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I'm sorry, Witness, but let me give you another example, contemporaneous example. Take the case of Iraq, for instance. Sometimes there are members of parliament, politicians who go on the ground, who visit the units, who talk to the members of the units. Does this mean that one is going to infer that this particular political party is commanding the operations on the ground? This is what the whole issue hinges on. These are some of the questions that the Bench have.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe I understand your -- your question, your concern. When you give the example of Iraq, you are talking about a regular armed force, probably one of the coalition forces active there, who are being visited by people who are not part of the chain of command. If a Member of Parliament or any other authority who is not part of the chain of command would visit these units and would give orders, there would be a problem, because the principle of single command and control would be violated. So in such a situation the person who receives the order has to inform his commander on the next superior level to alert him of this event. Returning to the report compiled by Zoran Rankic, deputy chief of the War Staff, Rankic is visiting a unit of SRS volunteers. On the 30th of August, 1991, he meets Branislav Gavrilovic. Branislav Gavrilovic is a senior SRS volunteer. I have been able to draw that conclusion from other documents I have reviewed while preparing this report, and you will notice that Gavrilovic, also known as Brne, is not only active in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem as a person in charge of SRS volunteers, but we also see him later in other areas, for example, Sarajevo in the course of 1992 and later on where he's in the same position, in command of a group or detachment of SRS volunteers. Gavrilovic is even recognised for his activities during the conflicts by Mr. Seselj through his proclamation to Chetnik Vojvoda. So what we have is a member of the SRS War Staff visiting a SRS unit in the area. To address your point about the JNA. As I said, the document does not allow to conclude who of the JNA was in charge. However when we look at the specifics, and that is also addressed in the Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem section of my report, the senior command of the JNA is unhappy with the situation in Eastern Slavonia at that moment in time. That is why in the course of the month of September the overall commander is replaced, i.e., that General Zivota Panic commander of the 1st military district is put in charge of the operations in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Panic, after his appointment reorganises the forces into two Operational Groups, Operational Group north, Operational Group south there are still other forces active too; but the main impact of Panic taking over is as he declares himself he installs or he restores single command and control over all the forces, JNA, TO Serbia, local Serb TO as well as volunteers that are active in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if we now go to the next document, which will then be 486. If we can call that up in e-court. This is a document saying -- well, there we have it up on the screen. Defence Staff document. Do you refer to this document also in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And what does this document tell us about orders and reporting within the SRS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In particular reporting to the War Staff.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, which was also published later on in the SRS party magazine includes detailed information on the military situation in Western Slavonia where SRS volunteers are active. It also addresses how this unit was trained, its activities, how it's structured, and at the end of the report -- maybe if we go to the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, we can do that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last paragraph, Your Honours, Radovanovic -- I'm reading from the document now. In the last -- in the second line of the last paragraph he says: "At 1800 hours the same day I dismissed all the volunteers under my direct command who were stationed in the villages," and so on and so on, "and ordered them to report to the Party Staff in Belgrade on their arrival at their places of residence ..." This shows that Radovanovic is in a position to issue orders and even he has volunteers under his command. There's no mention made of any notification or participation of a JNA officer or commander, commanding officer in that transfer of order, and then these volunteers are to report based on the order of Radovanovic to the SRS War Staff in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would seek the admission of the two documents we just have talked about, 459 and 486.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We'll give an a number, but then I will ask my question. So could you please give us two numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. 65 ter number 459 will be Exhibit number P221 under seal, and 65 ter number 486 will be Exhibit number P222 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. Expert witness, this report which was sent by Mr. Radovanovic to the Serbian Radical Party, apparently, seems to deal with the activities of the volunteers from the SRS. This report explains that the detachment was set up on July 7th in the village of Grosnica, and then describes what has happened, which is very well, but I have a question. I with like to know how this commander, Radovanovic, military-wise, who does he report to? Does he report to the JNA or is it a completely autonomous unit of -- similar to a paramilitary unit at work here, because page 5, paragraph 3, you know, nothing escapes me, he does mention a warrant officer 2nd class Vujanovic. Obviously he seems to belong to the JNA, and this person is supposed to be in charge of the mortar battery. This Vujanovic also seems to be connected to the TO in the village of Sodolovci. So military-wise we have combatants on the ground. There's combat activities going on, and there's a command. Now, that this one should report to his political party, why should he not make a report to the -- to his military party? Maybe they're military secrets, and that's another problem, of course. But you seem to say that with this report we have basis for foundation for the theory according to which the Serbian Radical Party is directly controlling armed forces on the ground, that this report is the true example and a perfect example and illustration of this. This is your theory. Fine. But -- but I would like to know exactly what is the situation of this unit before going along with your theory, because if for one -- in one way or another it is under JNA command, then I believe that your theory should be very closely scrutinised. And you are not telling us that as of July 7th, 1991, in this region, you're not telling us exactly what is the military structure that is in place, and I believe that this is missing, and this is creating a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the situation in Western Slavonia is discussed in a separate section in my report starting on page 124 of the second part of the report. Now, to answer your question, theoretically --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not dealing with Western Slavonia here at all but Eastern Slavonia. These are villages in Eastern Slavonia where the volunteers were before the JNA entered into armed combat with the Croatian paramilitaries. So we're dealing with Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is Eastern Slavonia. So please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, the conflict is in full development. At that stage, at the date of the document, 13th of September, 1991, as I mentioned in the previous reply to a question, the forces -- the forces in -- in Eastern Slavonia, there are problems with, among other things, command and control, and that's why on the level of the JNA measures are taken to restructure the forces in order to impose single command and control. Now, Srecko Radovanovic is a SRS volunteer. I have not found information on any position or rank he held within the JNA. To answer your question on the warrant officer, a warrant officer is not an officer but it's a senior non-commissioned officer. Well, the situation is such that at that moment in time in several areas as we have discussed in relation to the problems the JNA was facing with mobilisation and the call-up of reservists, there are even people within the JNA who -- who refuse to continue to serve in the JNA and, for example, here join a local Serb TO unit or even a volunteer unit. It is obvious that in theory the military hierarchy should have acted against that, but we cannot draw a conclusion for this specific person. Now, to further provide you information on the -- the situation in Eastern Slavonia, I have heard from officers of the Guards Motorised Brigade who were part of Operational Group south, so the Operational Group that was in charge of taking Vukovar, that the situation with the volunteers was such that one -- that on one day a whole group of volunteers could have disappeared even though while they were participating in the operation, they were under JNA command and control. The other thing could happen, too, that two days later suddenly there's a group of 500 volunteers who wish to -- who have been sent from Belgrade or from Serbia to participate in the fighting. So it is very hard to provide a sort concise answer that covers all the situations because we are in a very de facto situation at that moment in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, it is a complicated situation, and when a situation is complex, it's best not to draw hasty conclusions. If you look at the last page in this report, you see how complex it is. Look at the fourth paragraph before the end. He says it's 1400 hours. He's talking about a motorised unit of the JNA in Laslovo, the village of Laslovo. There's obviously a battle, and we know that JNA is present there. Next paragraph then we find out that five men were killed in the battle, two SCP volunteers, two members of Arkan's unit, and the commander of the defence of the village of Markusica. So when we scrutinise all this, we find out there are several units involved. Several people, not just SRS volunteers, other volunteers also and if there is a battle going on at one point in time there must be some kind of command and control in place. It seems that the JNA has a motorised unit present, so any logical mind must draw the conclusion that it is not chaos that is occurring there, but maybe it is, I don't know. But when I read this report, I note there are people from Arkan's unit, from other political parties. They're not just SRS volunteers. What can you say about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the situation should be that all the units would be under the command of the -- under the command of the -- the most senior JNA officer in the area. That is what the doctrine says. That is what the law says. However, as I've tried to explain, when we look at this particular report in context and we -- we study the events in Eastern Slavonia and the situation at that time, there is indeed -- I wouldn't call it chaos, but there are problems with ensuring single and unified command and control in the area. As Kadijevic pointed out in his book and we discussed it, the JNA's facing enormous problems with mobilisation and the call-up of reservists. At the same time there are political parties in Serbia who say, "Well, we don't trust the JNA because the JNA is Communist. We want to defend the Serbs so we send volunteers." Eastern Slavonia is the closest by area to Serbia. It's a direct border, the Danube River, to go and participate in the fight in their view to defend the Serbs. So there are volunteers or groups appearing in the area with their own internal structure like, for example, the group of Radovanovic. There are also other units in the area. The Serbs have established -- the local Serbs have established local Serb TO units which is here called the command of the defence of that village. There maybe barricades in some villages whereas in another village five kilometres further, nothing is happening. Just to -- I mean to -- to show to you the complexity of the situation, the senior command, I mean the Supreme Command Staff is aware of the situation and takes measures in the course of the months of September, at least for Eastern Slavonia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm trying to replace these volunteers within the framework of a military operation, and I note that you have not really worked in detail regarding this, and I'll demonstrate this to you. Go to page 6, paragraph before last -- before the paragraph -- the second paragraph before the end. There are platoons cropping here and there. So it seems that that is large-scale military operation underway, and there was an artillery operation that had been planned for 7.00, 0700 hours, with 120-millimetre mortars, and they shelled until 0800 hours. So everything was planned. This was not chaos. This was not improvised. This had been planned. So did you try and find the orders on the Croatian side on the JNA side? In order to really investigate the combat action to draw the conclusion, which if I follow your conclusion you're saying that on the ground there are only SRS volunteers that are under direct command of the Serbian Radical Party in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't want to create the impression that the conclusion you just mentioned that is my conclusion. My conclusion is that the report shows certain things about the SRS volunteers in the area. To answer the first part of your question, indeed we have sent -- when I say "we," the Office of the Prosecutor has sent numerous requests for assistance to first the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, then Serbia and Montenegro, and then Serbia in order to obtain orders, documents of JNA units in Eastern Slavonia and Baranja, yeah, in order to obtain these documents. I don't remember whether there was a specific document for this specific operation or whether we made a specific question for this specific operation; but I can assure you, and if required I can bring you a record of the requests we made that such requests have been made over at least the past six years. I have not been able to identify additional information which would allow to determine in further detail what was exactly happening in the area Radovanovic is talking about, but I believe that when taking -- when one looks to -- in context with the other documents I have quoted in the report, that this document assists in drawing the conclusion I draw, and I can repeat that conclusion. That is that this document shows that the Serbian Radical Party has volunteers active in the area of Eastern Slavonia. They are not the only volunteers. I haven't claimed that and that these volunteers enjoy particular relations with the Radical Party and the War Staff, whereby members of the War Staff can issue orders to these volunteers, and there is also an internal hierarchical structure within those SRS volunteers in the area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I must intervene, Judge, sir, because for quite some time this expert has been misleading you intentionally. This is the period where the JNA was not yet participating in the conflict. You see when at 1400 hours an armoured units of the JNA arrived the fighting stopped. The volunteers were helping the defence of Serbian villages and had nothing to do with the JNA, and yet the witness is referring to orders issued by the Supreme Command. Your Honour can say this can be dealt with in cross-examination but it's been going on for too long. This is the period in which the volunteers of the Serbian radical army did not have any links with the JNA. That's why they withdrew. They were defending individual Serbian villages in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you heard what's just been said. Would you like to respond or not, or are you waiting for the cross-examination? Yes, because the theory put forward by Mr. Seselj several times already, he states that in September already the JNA according to him is not one of the main parties to these operations and they might not even be there at all, and spontaneous defence systems were established either in the villages or by the TO. So this was then reinforced by volunteers. What do you have to say about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would reply the following way, that is already during the incidents in Borovo Selo which is not so far away from the villages discussed in this report, and I'm talking about the 2nd of May, 1991, the JNA is sent to separate the warring parties. The report sent by Radovanovic does not allow to draw the conclusion as to what the JNA is doing. It could well be that at this stage, so mid of September, some JNA units in particular areas where a conflict erupts are sent to separate the warring factions. I would just like to return to what I said earlier, that is that later on in the month of September the Supreme Command issues certain orders and it's at the latest on the 30th of September that we see the existence or written evidence of the existence of Operational Group south in Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the -- the issue we are dealing with here is the structure of the SRS, and many of these documents are referred to in detail in subsequent parts of the report. So what I'm trying to focus on here is really these structural issues. I'm sorry, we're blaming you, Mr. Theunens, for doing anything here, but there's a question I think arise with respect to this report which we should address. Now, bearing in mind that we should not in public session to reveal the source of the document, do you know from which archive this document come?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know by heart. I only -- all I know ask that -- no, I assume it comes from the party archives of the Serbian Radical Party, but I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll make submissions on that later on, but I do believe that this is correct, and in the B/C/S version of the document, if you look at the top you will see some of the information that we discussed yesterday in private session which identify which archive this come from. The point here being that this kind of report was actually sent to -- to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could I please finish my sentence before you I intervene? Thank you. That this document was available to the War Staff. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, evidently, evidently, Mr. President, the OTP has acquired this document illegally, and it didn't have to; but the OTP did not get this from the archives of the Serbian Radical Party. That's for sure. And there's no evidence they received it from the archives. They never asked for anything from the archives of the Serbian Radical Party. Had they asked for something, they might have got it or they might not, but they never asked. This is not a secret document. The Prosecutor has Exhibit 958. This was disclosed to us before this witness came to testify, and you see an article from issue number 12 of the Serbian Radical Party, dated February 1992, and the Prosecutor does not know about this even though they got it themselves and yet it's published in there. And yet they are presenting a document they acquired illegally. I'm not challenging the authenticity of this document, but I'm challenging its legality, the way in which it has acquired, and yet here you have it published periodical and even illustrated with photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We discovered that this report was published, and we also discover that this report was handed over to a member of the OTP. What matters is not how the report was communicated. What matters is what this report says. Mr. Marcussen, we have five minutes before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now, in terms of the structure and functioning the War Staff, the next issue I was going to attack with the witness, so to speak, is the issue of deployment of SRS volunteers. And again we, I think, have discussed some of these documents before, but what I'll try to do is to go through one, two, three -- seven documents relevant to this issue, ask briefly the expert to -- to explain the relevance of these documents, and then I'm going to seek the admission of the documents. I think in the interests of time it might be useful to get through the documents and then discuss the conclusion that is flow from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, first I'd like to look at Exhibit 609.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In which binder is this, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It is in -- in Your Honours' binder it's the next document in the binder that you have. I'm essentially moving through the tabs of the binder in the order that you find them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we now have the document up on the screen. Just briefly, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, but I can't find it here, 609.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 609 came after the report by Radovanovic. So after number 486. It's the document that comes right after that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And -- and it is displayed on the monitor. I also just read out what it is. It says: "Letter of authority. On behalf of the SRS volunteer unit, commander Radovan Novacic is hereby authorised to coordinate on behalf of the SRS with the Podravska Slatina TO staff and the staff of the Western Slavonia district on issues related to the defence, manpower, and other needs, in cooperation with the SRS Staff. The commander shall be recalled at the intervention of the SRS War Staff in Belgrade." And then the identification number of the person in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what does this show us about how volunteers were deployed on the ground and under whose authority they fell?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shows that the SRS War Staff is -- has the authority to appoint commanders to a group of SRS volunteers who are deployed on the field, and also to what is called coordinate on behalf of the SRS the activities of these volunteers with the local Serb Podravska Slatina TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if we move on to the next document which is 690. And again this would be the next document in the binder. We have here an order issued by the chief of the War Staff, and now we have it up on the screen. Mr. Theunens, is this a document that you've also used and does it show the same kind of authority by the War Staff?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document is used on page 134 of the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the next document I'd like the witness to look at is 657, and that also is marked for identification as P23. Again, Mr. Theunens, is this a document that illustrates the point you make about the manner in which SRS volunteers are being deployed on the ground?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And this specific document deals with the situation in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, just to follow through with these -- just to illustrate the type of documents and the regions they're being used in, the next document is 500 -- excuse me. That's incorrect. Is 782.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. Perhaps we could just keep this document on the screen for a short while, because this has to do with Vukovar and the Leva Supoderica detachment. Witness, this document is a document that stems from the Serbian Radical Party. Is addressed presumably to the commander of this detachment, and it seems that in the first paragraph we read that all the volunteers are placed under the command of this commander with a view to protecting Vukovar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document seems to be saying that the SRS War Staff has appointed Slobodan Katic, "a brave and experienced soldier from Belgrade," him commander of the volunteers in Vukovar. Is this what this document says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, in military terms what conclusions do you draw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Go we could scroll a little bit downwards to see the date of the document. So this document is dated 9th of November. At that moment the situation in Vukovar is as follows, and the details can be found in my report: We have as the main unit in the area south of the Vuka river, we have the Guards Motorised Brigade, which also constitutes the command of Operational Group south. Operational Group south constitutes of the Guards Motorised Brigade the 80th motorised brigade, units of the TO of the Republic of Serbia as well as --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down, Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. As well as local Serb TO units, including the TO Vukovar and the Leva Supoderica detachment. I mentioned yesterday that all these units are organised in an operational manner whereby the operation group consists of a number of Assault Detachment and the assault detachments consist of a number of assault groups. The assault groups more or less correspond with the JNA companies, i.e., companies of the guards moment raised brigade, but they are reinforced with other forces, local Serb TO, reservists and so on, including, for example, the Leva Supoderica detachment. So Leva Supoderica is part of a JNA-led assault group, but Leva Supoderica as such is a SRS volunteer detachment which is commanded by somebody of the SRS and somebody who had been appointed by the War Staff. Now, I know from the events in Vukovar that the command of the Guards Motorised Brigade was closely involved in the command structure of Leva Supoderica, and if, for example, they did not agree with a person being in command, then a member of -- or the command, at least the commander, but also other members of the command of OG south could intervene to replace the commander of Leva Supoderica. And I remember but this is not addressed in the report, that Slobodan Katic, who was first in charge of the TO Vukovar is replaced at one moment in time by a person known as -- it's Vujovic or Vujanovic, but the name is in my report. Okay, Milan Lancuzanin has been appointed by the SRS War Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well I shall stop you here because it's now time to have break. The hearing has gone on for an hour and a half already. We shall have a break and meet again at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note clarification of Judge Antonetti's comments it is hard to imagine a French person being against a German or North American being against a south American because of the civil war. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.34 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. A Judge has a question to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, I apologise because I'm a woman and maybe women are not very good until military matters, but out of these documents and out of your testimony I -- I understand, at least that's my personal opinion, that the Serbian Radical Party and its War Staff had authority, I don't know if it was military or political or maybe only moral, I don't know yet, but it had authority as regards the appointment of the units -- of the volunteer units, but then there's another problem at that comes to mind, and maybe you can shed some light on this to help me out. I would like to know whether the commander of the Volunteers Unit, which -- who had been appointed by this War Staff, by the SRS War Staff, was also officially -- had also officially been appointed by the TO, that's for the times when the JNA wasn't there yet, and later on by the JNA. So that's my first question. Then I have another question, which is still on the same document, the last one we saw. At one point in time you said that the Leva Supoderica detachment was part of the Assault Detachments of the JNA. Is this what I understood? So there were assault groups. Now, who was in command of these assault groups? Now you have my two questions, and I would like you to shed some light on this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, to answer the first question first, the people in charge of a SRS volunteer detachment were appointed or put in that position by the SRS War Staff. I have not come across examples whereby the JNA -- the JNA commander in the area removes that commander or appoints somebody else. Of course the matter is a bit more complicated. When we look at the unit in Vukovar at one point Slobodan Katic is the commander of the unit in Vukovar, and his name has appeared in earlier documents. However, even though commands of the TO should be appointed by the civil authorities according to the legislation as it is existed SFRY, we see at the latest on the 23rd or the 24th of November, based on the information I have seen, which is not included in this report, it is the JNA, and in that specific case Colonel Mile Mrksic, who was the commander of OG south who appointed Vujovic, Miroljub Vujovic to the position of commander of the TO, local Serb TO Vukovar. As far as the second question is concerned, indeed the command of the assault groups that are part of the assault detachments of Operational Group south in Vukovar, October, November 1991, were JNA officers. They were in fact, if I remember well, all company commanders within the JNA Guards Motorised Brigade at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an additional question to follow up. Unless I'm mistaken, right now out of all the witnesses that were called by the Prosecution, you are a military expert. Everything you're saying, of course, is of great importance, and we pay great attention to the questions asked and the answers given, and we will also pay great attention to your answers to Mr. Seselj during the cross-examination. Now, my fellow Judge has asked an absolutely essential question, which is the following: Who is -- has the final say in appointing these people, these volunteers from the SRS? So you answered from one aspect talking about the TO and the JNA. But while I was here listening, to you I was -- another idea came to my mind, especially when you know how Territorial Defence operated in all these republics of the former Yugoslavia where the municipal or regional criterion is extremely important, and so I wondered whether it was possible that in a given municipality X, with locals that would be there, would it be possible to suddenly have someone come up from Belgrade who have been appointed as commander of these locals? Here I think this -- this brings questions to mine. Let's imagine, for example, in Vukovar there's a lot of locals, and suddenly a commander would be sent from Belgrade to command those locals. So I think that this brings a question to mind in a -- in the framework of -- if it happened in the framework of a political appointment. Now, if there is an appointment that has been stamped by the JNA or later on by the VRS in BiH as of May 1992, then it's easier to understand that the military authority could impose commanders to the locals, but we were talking about Vukovar. It's in the indictment, and we will have to rule on this question later on. So regarding Vukovar, the commander of the Leva Supoderica detachment, a commander who had been appointed at first, could you confirm that he had been appointed by the TO, by the municipality, if I could say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the part of the complexity arises from the fact that what you point out is -- is hundred per cent correct but we are dealing with de facto structures. The TO in Vukovar is not the TO as it existed prior to the conflict, i.e., a TO unit which would respond to the authorities of the Republic of Croatia. In this particular case local Serbs have established their own TO unit in Vukovar. Milan Lancuzanin, who was the commander of Leva Supoderica, whereby Leva Supoderica is the name of a geographic area in Vukovar; he is a local. I have no information on the circumstances of his appointment, but I can mention, and that is reported -- that is included in my report, that he's confirmed as the commander of Leva Supoderica by the SRS War Staff. In the SRS party magazine Velika Srbija, it is also mentioned that Leva Supoderica is a Chetnik detachment. At one moment when Milan Lancuzanin is proclaimed Chetnik Vojvoda, and this is on page 119 in part 2 of my report, he is identified as the commander of the Leva Supoderica Volunteer Unit of the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Chetnik Movement. So even though Leva Supoderica is a unit of the local Serb TO, it is also identified in SRS documentation as a SRS document. And the complexity of the whole issue lies in the fact that we're talking about de facto units, self-established units which use de jure names like TO, but in fact they're something else. I'm not sure that answered your question, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So assuming that what you're saying is true and cannot be challenged, if we take the assumption that the SRS has authority to appoint commanders with those self-proclaimed TOs or those de facto TOs, let's assume that this is the case, but in terms of military -- in terms -- in terms of the military, I mean, these people, they're not Boy Scouts, you know, they're servicemen. They're soldiers, and they're supposed to fight with weapons, with ammunition. So what I would like to know is the following: In their military action, when they decide, you know, to carry out a military action, are they doing this under the authority and under the control and under the command and control of the SRS War Staff, or are they -- do they enjoy a great autonomy of action, or is this autonomy of action controlled either by the local TO, even if it's a self-proclaimed TO, or by the JNA, if the JNA is present? So what I would really like to know is the following: Is there a connection, not in terms of the appointment, but is there a connection a link as to the military action carried out locally, a link between the Serbian Radical Party and those people that are in the field? Let me give you an example. Let's say that in an area X a unit of the Serbian Radical Party with a commander that had been appointed by the SRS, who may even been a Vojvoda, who might have been made Vojvoda, if during military action he decides to attack Croats or Muslims or who knows what, capture prisoners, so launch a military action, is he doing this on the order and instruction given by the SRS? That's the crux of the problem. You know that in terms of military -- the military, you know, there's always planning, orders, and things just don't happen at random. So I would like to know the following: When there's a military action, is it done under the local command of people who might have been appointed, maybe so, by the SRS, or is it controlled by the staff of the -- 100 per cent by the staff of the SRS? This is absolutely essential here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to -- as an introduction, I would like to mention that this report and my testimony is based on the documents that can be found in the footnotes. So all I do is -- is explain what is mentioned in those documents. To explain -- to answer your question, the short answer is we have to look at the specific situation. As you pointed out, military action is normally -- or military activity is determined by orders, written or oral orders. Whenever we had written orders for the areas discussed in the report, they are included. From those, we can conclude that for what Vukovar is concerned, as long as OG south exists, and Leva Supoderica is part of OG south, the military operations are ordered by the commander, i.e., from the commander of OG south through the chain of command, to the command of the south group to which-- or in which Leva Supoderica is included. However, this subordination does not rule out that Leva Supoderica maintains certain contacts with the SRS War Staff. And these contacts can concern the exchange of operational information, requests for promotion, and related matters. When we look at Western Slavonia, however, the matter is more complicated, because there we see, and I'm summarising what is actually discussed in detail in the report, that there are close contacts between the local Serb TO staffs -- staffs of various municipalities and also the regional local Serb TO staff on one hand and the SRS War Staff on the other hand, for example, for the provision of manpower for the local Serb TO in Western Slavonia. And in the exchange of information we see that the SRS War Staff imposes certain conditions to the local Serb TO before the volunteers of the SRS can be sent. We can also see from these documents that it is the SRS War Staff who appoints people who are to be in charge of these volunteers. I make a leap now to Bosnia-Herzegovina, to the situation in Sarajevo after May 1992, where we see that the relationship between SRS volunteer detachments in Sarajevo, and there are four, and we will discuss them later, and the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps is, to say the least, complicated because there is one example -- or there are several examples where the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps complains about the behaviour of SRS volunteers. However, when General Mladic, chief of the Main Staff of the VRS, orders to arrest one of the SRS volunteers, and I'm talking now about Vasilije Vidovic, also known as Vaske, the local VRS commander says, well, actually there's no need to arrest him because he is very useful doing operations. And Vaske clearly been appointed not by the VRS but by the SRS War Staff. And maybe one last element you spoke about that these were all people with military background. I just would like to point out that, for example, in Vukovar Lancuzanin, in an article in Velika Srbija, was described as a carpenter, and Miroljub Vujovic was a taxi driver. They were -- they obviously did their military service but they didn't have the same level of military education and training as JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give the floor to my fellow Judge because she has a question, and then to Mr. Seselj, who wants to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness, please one last question. You're talking about self-proclaim, de facto, so regarding the TO in Krajina controlled by the "Serbian rebels." So I'd like to know whether the Serbian law wasn't still applied there? It wasn't on the Serbian TO, on the deployment of volunteers and so on? So you're saying de facto, but de facto in relation to the authority that Croatia could have had, is that it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe for the record I can reply that indeed the authorities of the SAO Krajina in August 1991 adopted a decision to apply the law of defence of the Republic of Serbia on the territory of the SAO Krajina. And if I remember well, similar decisions were taken in the SAO SBWS. So when I use de facto as the Judge pointed out from the point of view of the Croatian authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Mr. Marcussen. You will have the floor, but Mr. Seselj would like to say something on a particular topic, and I know which one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have three brief objections, Judges. I couldn't interrupt you when you were putting your questions, but answering your questions off the top of his head, the witness overstepped by far the content of his expert report. He went far beyond it. There are things that he said which are not contained in the report and for which there is no evidence. He said at one point Slobodan Katic was the head of the Territorial Defence. This concerns Vukovar he has no evidence to support this, please ask him to provide it; further he said that the Serbian Radical Party confirmed the command of Milan Lancuzanin Kameni over the Leva Supoderica detachment. Please ask the witness to provide evidence for this. And thirdly, he has just stated that the War Staff of the Serbian Radical Party appointed Vasilije Vidovic Vaske as the commander of the volunteers in Vogosca and Ilijas. Please ask him to provide any evidence he may have to support this. He has to base these claims on evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Admittedly these are questions that could be put during cross-examination, but to try and see where we stand, because this is rather complex, I think it is better that the witness answers straight away. Now, you have understood as far as Mr. Katic is concerned, who according to you had been appointed commander of this detachment, what did you base this on? Now, as far as Kameni is concerned, he seemingly also would have been appointed by the SRS. Which document can you put forward in support of this? And the third point which had to do with Vidovic, once again what evidence do you have to support that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the first question, Your Honours, the position of Slobodan Katic as commander of the TO, I remember that TO Vukovar from the evidence that was given in the Vukovar trial. However, from 65 ter number 657 that was discussed earlier today, which is an a SRS War Staff document, it states that Slobodan Katic is the commander of the volunteers in Vukovar. There is also 65 -- excuse me, MFI P25, which states that Katic is the Chetnik commander Vukovar, whereby to come back to a previous question you asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, as far as Slobodan Katic is concerned, this document which I have before me, 657, it does state that he is commander of the volunteers, but he don't state that he is the commander of the detachment. Do you understand the difference? It's not quite the same to -- when you're commander of volunteers unit and a commander of a detachment, that's not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... may, Mr. President. Now the witness is refers to a document signed by Katic as the Chetnik commander for Vukovar. You may recall that this is a document dating from the time after the liberation of Vukovar when Katic remained to live in Vukovar. When Goran Stoparic testified we established this definitely. So the document dates from the period after the liberation of Vukovar, not during the fighting for Vukovar. The man stayed there. He remained residing there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which documents -- document appoints Katic commander of this unit? Not after the fact, not after the events in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will try and clarify. I remember from the evidence that was presented in the Vukovar trial that Slobodan Katic was the commander of the local Serb TO in Vukovar until sometimes in October or November 1991. And for those who would like to see the details about that, I think there is the testimony of Katic as a Defence witness in that trial. What I've done afterwards, I referred to 65 ter number 657, which dates from the 9th of November, 1991. Just to clarify, Vukovar fell on the 18th, so this is amidst the operations. This document states that the SRS War Staff has appointed Slobodan Katic as the commander of the volunteers in Vukovar. So I hope -- this is the information I can provide in relation to Katic. The relation -- the information in relation to Lancuzanin, I would have to look in my report to give you the concrete reference. But, for example, on page 117 -- on English page 117 in part 2, mention is made of an interview with Branislav Vakic, who was also a senior SRS volunteer when he talks about the fact that one group of Chetniks had already been deployed on the approach to Vukovar -- or to the town, but it's Vukovar, under the command of Milan Lancuzanin. Furthermore, there is a reference -- when you look at the order for the -- as I mentioned, the proclamation of Lancuzanin to Chetnik Vojvoda, his title is described as commander of the Leva Supoderica Volunteer Unit of the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Chetnik Movement. My understanding was that Lancuzanin, having already living -- or living already in Vukovar prior to the start of the operations established his own unit, but thanks to his links with the SRS, he obtained additional manpower. So not only volunteers but volunteers from -- volunteers from Vukovar but also people from outside Vukovar, in particularly Serbia. And based on the fact that Milan Lancuzanin is mentioned as the commander of Leva Supoderica in several SRS documents, I concluded from that that he was confirmed as the commander of Leva Supoderica by the SRS. Coming now to Vaske, we would have to go to the Sarajevo section in part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll get back to Kameni. In any case, this man Kameni, if nobody calls him to testify, the Trial Chamber can ask this gentleman to come and testify. That said, we know that Kameni is a person from Vukovar. He wasn't sent by Belgrade. He was from Vukovar. We know that he becomes the commander of that detachment, but he might have become commander without the SRS, the Serbian Radical Party, having had a hand in this. He might have been a commander before his personal merits, which I think I acknowledged by the Serbian Radical Party that appoint him Vojvoda. Very well. But as far as Kameni is concerned, this person may have developed his career inside the unit without this necessarily having had anything to do with the SRS, and the SRS may have had nothing to do with his promotion in the military, but his sheer qualities were such that the SRS decided to appoint him and give had him this title of Vojvoda. It is very difficult -- it is difficult for us to understand what is going on, because depends from which angle you look at it, of course, and the consequences aren't the same. If you put yourself in the shoes of the SRS and he is the man who is running the show, this means, of course, that his responsibility can be alleged, or we're talking about a political party that is playing a political role, a moral role, whatever you want to call it, but where command structure is separate and not under his control. Therefore, there are two alternatives which can be taken into account here. Which alternative do you choose?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a short comment. The Prosecution is intentionally hiding an important document here. The document will show me while I was testifying in the Milosevic trial, and it is an order by the commander of the 1st Guards Mechanised Motorised Brigade or commander of Sector South for the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party to be deployed in the Leva Supoderica detachment. The Prosecutor has that document but doesn't wish to show it in this trial, whereas it was shown in the previous trial. The commander of the 1st Guards Brigade issued an order that the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party coming to Vukovar should go to the Leva Supoderica detachment, and I'm sure that this expert witness had that document in his hands too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, can you answer my question and in fact in Mr. Seselj's comment, in other words, a document was tendered in the Milosevic trial, document which pertained in this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents I reviewed do not allow to conclude how Milan Lancuzanin, also known as Kameni, became the commander of Leva Supoderica. However, the documents show that Leva Supoderica is a Chetnik detachment, and this document I'm citing is an article which was published in Velika Srbija titled "Serbian Vukovar will live on." On page 108 of the second part of the report, I mention a handwritten letter bearing a stamp of the Vukovar TO which deals with and I quote, "The legalisation of the functioning of the unit detachment Leva Supoderica." This letter is 65 ter number 590. In the letter it is also stated that Milan Lancuzanin will be the commander of Leva Supoderica. Now, when I said earlier that I don't -- I cannot establish the circumstances for the appointment of Lancuzanin, I mean -- I meant by that that I have not been able to find information on the person who signed the letter in 65 ter number 590. We know it's a Dusan Filipovic, but I have not been able to find more information on that person, as I said. To answer Mr. Seselj's question, I -- I would be very happy to see the document. It may well be that it has been presented in the Milosevic trial, but I don't remember that I came across this document while preparing for this report. Now, if we can show the document during cross-examination I think that would be very helpful in order to establish its importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure he will do that, I assume. Now, the third point. The -- Vidovic's position.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We would have to go to the Sarajevo section in my report which starts the second part English page 220. Now, I think the best information on the links between Vidovic and the SRS could be found in -- I only have the 65 ter number, but 65 ter number 2030, which the Chetnik Vojvoda proclamation order because it will include a short CV of Vidovic, but I don't remember the exhibit number it has received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It is P218, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I think the best would be to have a look at that document and then we can all see from the document what the CV of Vidovic is as well as his relation with the SRS War Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's try and move on, please. Mr. Marcussen, I'm sorry if we ask these questions, but we have all understood that military issues are extremely important, and for the time being we have the witness in front of us, the expert witness in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, and I hope he is of assistance to -- to the Court. I believe I have you've used less than three of the five hours that I have with the witness, so I'm just concerned whether we're going to have the witness survive this, but we will move on quickly. Your Honours, we were on the issue of deployment of volunteers, and I believe we had reached Exhibit number 782, which maybe we can also call up on the screen. Now, this is a document that I think we can pass fairly quickly. It's an authorisation from the War Staff for the purpose of establishing law and order and control in Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you have the document in front of you, is this one of these documents that you have also looked at with respect to the issue of deployment of volunteers and, if so, what does it show?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. This document is also included in my report. The document shows that the chief of the SRS War Staff has the authority to appoint somebody, in this case a Milan Dobrilovic, to establish law and order and control in Western Slavonia. He is also authorised to supervise all the volunteers in cooperation with a Colonel Jovan Trbojevic in command of the Territorial Defence. Now, in the section, Western Slavonia, in my report I explained that Jovan Trbojevic is a JNA officer who has been appointed to be the command of the local Serb Territorial Defence in Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, the next three exhibits go together, so if Your Honours would bear with me while I go through the three documents with the witness. I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Witness, my colleague was telling me something which is important. This document which we have before us which shows that Milan Dobrilovic is -- has a particular position. This document clearly shows that he needs to work in cooperation with the commander of the Territorial Defence. He's not the big boss. A colonel is also there. And furthermore, if you look at the title of the document, it is not an order. It says "Authorisation." I don't know that -- what this might tell us. This could also be for information purposes or a statement or proclamation or -- it doesn't say "Order," an order that needs to be put into effect. What we can see is that Dobrilovic has been given powers by the SRS, but this doesn't mean that there is a military connection between the SRS and the local unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the -- the use of the word "Authorisation" in a written document to me shows that Milan Dobrilovic can use it almost as a letter of authority. This document shows that Dobrilovic has authority. So if -- when he goes to Western Slavonia and even if he collaborates with Jovan Trbojevic. Well, when he go and see the SRS volunteers in the area he can use this document to tell them, "Look, I have been sent by the SRS War Staff --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another question, a follow-up question. We have several documents that are issued by the Serbian Radical Party. So far no one has put a question about this. I was waiting to get more information before putting the question. Now that we have this document before us, let's look into the reasons why Milan Dobrilovic was appointed here. This is with a view to establishing law, order, and control. That is the reason why, law, order, and control, and we have a swathe of documents that are issued by the SRS; and these always refer to law, discipline, reminders of the law, and every time I look at all these documents, I might be right, I might be wrong, I have the feeling that the Serbian Radical Party was extremely concerned about the fact that these "volunteers" should respect law, order, and anybody who failed to comply with disciplinary measures had to be notified to the SRS. In all these documents, we always see that there is a reminder of this, and this is particularly striking, because this is the object of this authorisation. Through military action to capture prisoners, not to capture people, but enemy soldiers. It does not say that one should -- this is a -- for Dobrilovic the obligation to have law and order respected. It's not a matter of attacking people, capturing people, killing, or affecting the integrity of people or of people's property. All the documents we have seen are in the same vein. So have you noticed this or has this escaped you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I'm very conscious of that, but I would like to clarify focusing on three aspects. First of all in the military in very general terms in an order has to be repeated several times like for example even if it's an authorisation but still this emphasis on the requirement to establish law and order, it means that there is a problem, because otherwise there's no need to repeat or to reissue orders. So the fact that this aspect is re-emphasised several times to me would first show there is a problem. Secondly, that's maybe more related to the testimony here, there are many more documents included in the report. We have obviously -- or the Prosecutor has obviously only chosen a few ones. I can assure you that in the document -- in the report I also have documents from JNA officers in the same area who actually complain about the behaviour of SRS volunteers and who refer to the commission of crimes like looting, burning of houses and other serious crimes which they include in their reports to their superiors and where they sometimes ask their superiors to do something about it. And if you wish so, I can point some of these documents out, but for Western Slavonia, for example, on page 137 and following, especially on page 138, we have the -- the MFI P187 and related to that we have 65 ter number 958 and 933, where the involvement or the alleged involvement of an individual known as Jovan Kulic, who according to an SRS publication was a member of the Kragujevac Chetnik detachment, whereby Kragujevac is an important city in Serbia, and so there are various documents from -- from the military as well as from the military prosecutor on involvement of Kulic in crimes, whereby Kulic is also identified as a self-proclaimed captain who robbed and looted in Western Slavonia in -- in a 5th JNA corps confidential document which corresponds with 65 ter numbers 933.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're absolutely right. There is a great deal of documents showing that volunteers of the SRS may have committed crimes that may be described as criminal. No one denies that. It's obvious. But what we find is that the SRS, on numerous occasions, reminds everyone that there are crimes committed, that measures need to be taken, that law and order need to be re-established. It's not an encouragement to continue with these things. In any army you have black sheep, including in the best and most famous armies in the world. You always have them. And this is even more so when you're dealing with volunteers who have not been properly trained or educated and who might be tempted to commit crimes. The impression I get is that after a number of crimes were committed and everybody was aware of these crimes, a general conclusion is -- is drawn, that is that all SRS volunteers are criminals, and therefore that -- the fact that crimes were committed comes as no surprise. That seems to be the theory you develop in your report. It might be the case. It might not be the case. We would need to look into these crimes very thoroughly to determine whether that is the case or not, but does this necessarily mean that the SRS was the one who gave the orders for these crimes to be committed in the field? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said before, the report is based on documents. I have not come across a document where, for example, the Serbian Radical Party orders volunteers to commit crimes. I would find that quite unusual to put that in a document. Now, I think whether the volunteers are more likely to commit crimes than ordinary soldiers, that's a matter where I have an opinion and views based on my military experience, but I have not addressed that in my report. So if you wish, I could elaborate on that, but it's not addressed in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. What matters for the Judges is the following: We have all these documents issued by the SRS. Are these documents that encourage the volunteers of the SRS to respect law and order, or are these documents that encourage them to commit crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that it -- it's not possible to categorise these documents, the SRS documents I have reviewed in such a way. There are indeed documents like this one to -- that call for establishing law and order and control, but I could also say that actually law and order and control only addresses the situation among the SRS volunteers and not law and order in general as we would understand it. In addition, in the report when discussing the situation in Vukovar and also the -- the role of Milan Lancuzanin, I have included some quotations of an article from the party magazine of the SRS, from Velika Srbija, whereby the -- the treatment of a prisoner of war is being discussed in rather graphic terms. And this article can be found on page -- English page 122 in the second part of the report, and this article corresponds with 65 ter number 957. And, okay, Velika Srbija is the official party magazine whereby Mr. Seselj is the founder and the editor of the magazine. And the article I mentioned doesn't make a direct call to commit crimes, but the information that is mentioned does not suggest a call to respect law and order or to abide by the Geneva Conventions pertaining to the treatment of prisoners of war either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. That's what you say. We'll probably come back to that later. Mr. Marcussen, I know that you've used up three hours. You have two hours left. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As another name was mentioned, Judge, I think that the witness is duty-bound to provide information straight away since Jovo Ostanic [phoen] was a member of the Serbian Radical Party and whether he was in Vukovar as a volunteer of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the accused is commenting and -- and requesting the witness for information which he can lead during his part of the examination. This is not proper for the accused to intervene in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj. You'll come back to that issue during cross-examination. The Trial Chamber has been very flexible so far, but the problem is that we'll use a lot of time if you keep making interruptions, and then there could be -- an imbalance between the two parties. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The next three documents, as I mentioned, go together. They are in your binder next to each other. The first one is 65 ter number 570. Mr. Theunens, is this -- this is a request for reinforcement, and I think you have already explained these three documents when you testified last week. Could you briefly tell us what is it these next three exhibits show, and then we will walk through them afterwards.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these three documents show an exchange of information between the Podravska Slatina local Serb TO staff and the Serbian Radical Party War Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It's in binder 1, Your Honours, towards the end.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I will repeat --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So these three documents represent an exchange of information between the Podravska Slatina so Western Slavonia local Serb TO staff and the SRS War Staff for the provision of manpower to the Podravska Slatina local certain TO by the SRS War Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I believe you mentioned these yesterday, or on Thursday last week. So the first document, 570, is a request for volunteers. Then the next document, 582, I believe you have mentioned this is a response, and I am correct, what you have noted here this is a document where certain conditions are put on the deployment of volunteers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. So the deputy chief and the SRS War Staff replies to the request, and he says, "Well we can fulfil the request provided that three conditions are fulfilled." They deal with technical matters, but also the third point, "coordination with our unit command," and "our" then refers to the SRS volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And am I correct that this is one of these type of documents that you refer to to illustrate that SRS units deployed were -- had an internal command structure and then dealt with either Territorial Defence or JNA, so to speak, toward the outside --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... a leading question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This has been answered several times and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Objection. You can't ask questions that way. I am warning you. You can't pose leading questions, and I have the right to interrupt you and object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, apparently your question was a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The expert is an expert witness. He has already set out this in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But anyway, Mr. Theunens, what conclusion do you draw from this kind of document as to the relationship between the internal organisation of the SRS units and the command structure they might be fitting into above the unit so to speak?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the conclusion I draw from this and actually we addressed that earlier is that even though during operations these volunteers are subordinate to the JNA or they are part of the local Serb TO, they still maintain certain relations, certain links with the War Staff, and I would just like to refer in this context to the document we discussed earlier today whereby Zoran Rankic went on a fact-finding mission to Western Slavonia on the orders of Mr. Seselj and the War Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then, Your Honours, if we turn to the next document which is number 594.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I believe, Mr. Theunens, this is then the document you referred to in your report as being the acceptance of Mr. Rankic letter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, Your Honours. So the local Serb TO staff in Podravska Slatina accepts the conditions imposed by Zoran Rankic and also provides information on how this would be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, this is the end of the documents I'm going to show the witness on the specific issue of the manner of deployment of the volunteers, and I'd like now to ask for the admission of the following exhibits, and I'd like to request that they be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we -- before we move into the question of admission of these documents, if I could just ask the witness to turn back to Exhibit 65 ter -- sorry, not exhibit but 65 ter number 582. Thank you. The third condition which is being put by Mr. Zoran Rankic that the TO establishes "coordination with our unit command," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will start with -- with the definition as it existed in JNA doctrine of coordination. Coordination does not imply subordination, but coordination is imposed by superior command.
