For example, if two battalions of a brigade have to coordinate their activity or their operations, this coordination will be imposed by the brigade commander, and it will be aimed at harmonising the activity. So that's the military significance of coordination. Now, Zoran Rankic also uses the word "coordination," drawing the parallel with the military definition. One could conclude that Rankic asks the TO staff in Podravska Slatina to harmonise its activities -- excuse me, to harmonise the activities of the Podravska Slatina TO staff and the activities of the SRS volunteer unit that is the command -- excuse me, the command of the SRS volunteer unit that is about to be deployed. Now, how this was done in practice, I would then like to refer you to the other documents in Western Slavonia -- on Western Slavonia that is discussed in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. We have seen those, but it still leaves at least me with an unclear impression of the command relations in the TO after the arrival of the volunteers from SRS. Apparently the volunteers kept their own unit command, and Mr. Rankic puts up as a condition for the dispatchment of these volunteers that the TO unit coordinates with the unit command. In practical terms, Mr. Theunens, how would this work out? Who would give the orders to organise the combat activities in which these volunteers would take part, and who would be in command of the time and the manner and the place where the attacks should be launched?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, normally there would be single command, and if JNA and TO were in the same area, the JNA commanding officers would be in command. Now, the SRS volunteers that are being sent are part of a separate unit which is a sub-unit of a higher-level unit whereby, similar as it was in Vukovar, they are pat of the chain of command. So the SRS volunteers are part of the TO and receive the orders for combat activity or actions and operations from the next upper level in the TO/JNA chain of command. However, this document, similar as the others, also indicates that even though they are subordinated to the TO or even part of the TO, they maintain particular relations with the SRS War Staff. Now, I have not seen an example of the SRS War Staff issuing an order for dealing with operational matters. For example, like tomorrow you will attack village X. I have not seen that. However, from JNA documents I have seen that they stated, well, at one day the volunteers withdrew or they left. Now, we cannot rule out that they left or withdrew out of their own initiative, but it's more likely that actually they withdrew or they undertook a certain activity following orders from the SRS War Staff if there were no orders from the JNA, because in the military activities and operations imply orders. So -- and if it's not the JNA who orders, it has to be another body that has -- that is in a position to order. And a document like this one suggests that the SRS War Staff is in such a position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question of my fellow Judge is very similar to my concerns. I think we should look again at this document. It is essential. If we've understood what you've told us so far, you know, and of course with all the documents we've seen so far, it seems that the Serbian Radical Party in 1991, let's take October, for example, since we have a document dating October, this party has the possibility of sending volunteers on the field. That's something we know. Then second, this may be contested, there are documents going in one direction, documents going in the other direction, but if need be the SRS can supply weapons and some logistics. So I think this is carved in stone. Okay. So let's take a look at this document we have here. We have this Mr. Rankic addressing himself to the Territorial Defence of this municipality, of the municipality of Podravska Slatina, and this is what he's saying, calling them dear brothers, which probably means they're very close, but this is what he's saying: He fully understands the problems that they are facing, and he adds, "In order to help you, you must meet a number of criterion, certain conditions," and there are three conditions. "We want to know what is the situation regarding food, logistics. We want to be -- we want to know about weapons, disposition of troops on the terrain, and we also want to know about the coordination with our unit command," which is probably the War Staff. And Mr. Rankic asks, "If you can fulfil all these conditions, we will supply you with the men you need, volunteers." As far as I'm concerned, these documents seem to show that the SRS can provide assistance in terms of men, maybe also in terms of resources, but not at any condition. They want to assess the situation first to see whether this assistance should be sent out or not. So here it's obvious that the SRS will provide help and assistance. Now, helping does not mean that -- in military terms, you know, that they're also going to be in charge of command and control and, furthermore, of directing the military operations. Do you agree with this or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. One last question now. Have you ever found documents that would set out that the SRS played a role to trigger off or maybe to direct or to control or to command the military actions that were carried out on the ground through planning, through risk assessment, through mobilisation of forces, because on their own, you know, these volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party wouldn't be enough. So do you -- have you ever found documents that would really establish that the SRS played a driving role in the decision-making process when it comes to military operations that were carried out on the ground? Let's not talk about Vukovar. I don't think you can answer the question using Vukovar, because we know that there was some kind of control, and the -- it wasn't the SRS that directed the military operation on the ground. You said yourself that there was a unity of command there. Did you find documents that really set out, establish, that the SRS not only assisted the TOs, you know, through logistical help, resources or men, but actually played a role in directing or triggering off the military operations regarding these volunteers that were set out on the ground? I mean, we've been coming back to this for days now, but this is really of the essence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand the importance of this issue, and I'm afraid I'm going to provide the same reply that I gave earlier, that is that I have not seen documents where the SRS War Staff or anybody else from the SRS issues orders for specific, call it tactical or operational matters. Like, for example, as we have JNA orders for Vukovar to attack part X, Y, Z of the city. I have not seen such documents. However, I have attempted to include in the report documents that show that the SRS doesn't only recruit and assist in the dispatching of volunteers but also, as you mentioned the word "control," control can be seen in the term "inspection," i.e., to see to what extent an order has been implemented. We spoke this morning about the report Zoran Rankic sent to the SRS War Staff following the order he had received from Mr. Seselj and the SRS War Staff to carry out a fact-finding mission in Western Slavonia. Now, if -- I mean to me at that suggests that even -- no. I apologise. I would rephrase that. If the volunteers had been ordinary volunteers as foreseen in the law, there would be no reference to the political party these volunteers belonged to. They would just have been ordinary volunteers, would be integrated into existing JNA or TO units. We see that the emphasis is late on the fact these are SRS volunteers. In most of the JNA documents I have seen or VRS documents where we talk about or SRS volunteers are mentioned, the fact they belong to the SRS is emphasised by indicates to me that this is linked, this allegiance has an importance. The documents I have included in the report also show that members of the SRS War Staff or senior SRS volunteers are called commanders of the SRS volunteers in a number of areas where these volunteers are active, for example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But these volunteers, did you -- do you have a figure for them? Do you know how many there were in 1991, 1992? Could you give us an assessment? It's probably going to be a ballpark figure, but how many are they, 1.000, 10.000, 100.000? Could you give us some --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Could you give us a figure because this is not an innocent question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say that less than 1.000 whereby I would like to emphasis that we see that volunteers, some volunteers move from area to area, and this is in particular to the situation with people who are proclaimed Vojvoda later. So for example somebody like Branislav Gavrilovic, excuse me, is first active in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, then we see him in Northern Bosnia then we see him in Sarajevo so even this 1.000 it doesn't mean 1.000 different volunteers it's probably much less even though the estimates by the SRS are much higher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you assess their number altogether as being a thousand at most.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be a good estimate, yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, I was asking this question because this morning I was looking at the Krajisnik judgement where there's a paragraph on the paramilitary units operating in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Out of memory, it's -- they said there were about 60 of them in that judgement representing altogether 4.000 to 5.000 people. So for these SRS you're telling me that there are a thousand altogether? So according to you since you're the expert, you're number one expert at the OTP regarding these issues, so it would be in Bosnia-Herzegovina do you think there were about 5.000 to 6.000 people that were attached to paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, when you give that figure it's on one side, the Serbian side in the conflict, or all parties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, just Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible. I have not studied all the groups that are known as paramilitaries, but it's possible. I wouldn't come up with a higher estimate, because in particular on the 28th of July, 1992, after the -- Colonel Tolimir provides a report on paramilitaries and volunteers, so Colonel Tolimir of the Main Staff of the VRS, provides a report on paramilitaries and volunteers, and this is followed by an order from the level of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to subordinate all paramilitaries or volunteers to the VRS or to have them disarmed. So -- which means that the figure is probably address the situation, yeah, prior to this order or the situation between 1992 and 1995. So a global total.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question, because I would like to hand the floor back to Mr. Marcussen. We talk at length about these Serbian volunteers, you know we've been talking about them for hours now, and I'm sure it's not about to end, but a thousand persons? Is it marginal or is it a significant number in relation to the conflicts that occurred in Croatia, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, maybe even Vojvodina? Is it a marginal number or is it an essential number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you would allow me I would like to ask from which context. In which context do you mean marginal or important whether it's from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Military-wise. Military-wise in combat, you know, in combat between factions, warring factions. Let me give you an example just to give you a few figures that come to mind. The 3rd Corps in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the BiH 3rd Corps represents more than 125.000 soldiers. So what's a handful of volunteers? A thousand volunteers, is it marginal, 1.000 compared to 120.000? That's the type of comparison I'm looking at. So these volunteers that we are talking at length about, military-wise was there an important component or was it just a marginal component?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will refer to the JNA documentation I have reviewed whereby most of the JNA documentation where commanders expressed their views on volunteers. They have a negative view on volunteers and state, well, their contribution to the combat is almost marginal or non-existent. However, General Miriksic [phoen], he praised the volunteers after the fall of Vukovar. General Biorcevic he considered Arkan and his people heroes because they continued where the members of the JNA refused to continued. We discussed earlier from Vaske Vidovic that General Mladic said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on. Arkan is not the SRS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honours. I'm giving a general reply, volunteers without making any reference to whether -- to their allegiance. So in summary JNA and VRS documentation rather negative assessment. On the other hand, even if the combat, the impact or the combat role of these volunteers is limited, I think one should never underestimate the motivational aspect of the whole issue of volunteers. Volunteers and in particular the SRS volunteers or Serbian volunteers and particularly the SRS volunteers are fighting for what they call the Serbian cause. Officially, they are fighting to liberate or to protect the Serbs. This almost brings us to a question you raised earlier, Your Honours, about guerrilla warfare. Guerrilla armies are in general much smaller than conventional armies but they have one strength, they have the strength of ideology and ideology as Mao said is actually much more important than structure or weapons. I would even expand that statement to Serbian volunteers because they're also fighting for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm stopping you here because we have a problem with Mao Tse-tung, Mao Zedong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The importance of ideology and especially for the volunteers that their motivation or their ideology is the key issue and when it comes to criminal behaviour, it's not a matter of how many people are involved but mainly what they are doing and for what purposes they are using this ideology, and I think that is the key issue in the whole matter we're discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's say out of a thousand Serbian volunteers, which is a ballpark figure, according to you and according to all the documents that you have perused, reports and so on, how many committed crimes, 10 per cent, 20 per cent, 50 per cent? Is there an order of magnitude? Ballpark figure again. You know, that would give us an ideas to whether it was marginal or essential.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I haven't conducted any research, conducted any statistical research, so I wouldn't be able to answer that question. I can only refer to JNA and VRS documents where they emphasise the involvement of volunteers in crimes but there are no statistical data or studies as you are looking for included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have no data to give us and you established no comparisons with crimes that were committed by the other warring factions. This was not part of your survey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I've had statistics in my training and I think all starts and ends with the accuracy of your data and having no access to accurate data I don't have an overall overview of all the crimes that were committed or not in the conflict and by which parties. So even if I would have attempted, I don't think it would be relevant to come up with such a guess, actually, because it would be highly inaccurate due to the absence of accurate data or figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I continue now on the -- with some documents relating to the arming and equipping -- equipment given to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for reminding me. Before we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have lost sight of what is most important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now I would like to request the admission under seal of the following documents: 609; 690; 657, which is also MFI P23; 782; 570; 582; and 594.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are all the documents which we have discussed in the presence of the witness; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, before I move on to the next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You had some objections.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As all these are public documents of the Serbian Radical Party and only the source from which the documents arrived in the OTP is suspect, I demand that all these documents be available to the public in full. There is no reason for them not to be available to the public, because there is general agreement that we will not investigate the manner in which the OTP came by these documents. Everybody mentioned in the documents is a public figure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless I'm mistaken, none of these documents have been asked to be tendered under seal. 609, 690, 670, yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So Mr. Seselj, as far as what you've just said is concerned, the Trial Chamber has decided to rule on this after your cross-examination. So we shall then see which documents will be made public and which documents will nonetheless remain under seal. I cannot answer right now. I cannot respond to your question whether these will be admitted under seal or not, but we can already give an exhibit number of these documents, registrar please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 609 will be Exhibit number P223. 690 will be Exhibit number P224, 65 ter number 653 will be P23 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please start again because there's a mistake. Please from the beginning again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. 65 ter number 609 will be Exhibit number P223, 65 ter number 690 will be Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 609 will be Exhibit number P223; 65 ter number 690 Exhibit number P224; 65 ter number 657 will be Exhibit number P23; 65 per number 782 will be Exhibit number P225; 65 ter number 570 will be Exhibit number P226; 65 ter number 582 will be Exhibit number P227; and 65 ter number 594 will be Exhibit number P228 all provisionally under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Marcussen, before the break we have five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, the next topic I would like to move into concern the arming and equipping of volunteers. Before we did go into the actual documents, who -- how -- how were the volunteers, the SRS volunteers, armed and equipped based on your analysis?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on the documents I have reviewed for the report the SRS volunteers received their weapons and equipment from three organisations consisting of the JNA, the Ministry of Interior the Republic of Serbia and also the ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would like now to do as last time, move through the tabs as they come in the binder. In the interests of time, I'll pass 1913, so the first document I'll ask you to look at is 1804. A lot of these documents are very short --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, I was waiting for this document 1913 to come up. I don't think I can overlook this. I don't think the Prosecutor should be allowed to just skip over it because there's nothing here to show who drew this document up, where, when, what the date is, what does it mean? It looks as if the Prosecutor might have a composed it himself. I think I have right to have the meaning of this document explained to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well I need to find document 1913 in my binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let's look at document 1913 on the screen, please. Mr. Marcussen, this document 1913, where does it come from, how did you get it, and so on and so forth, since this has been disputed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the accused is making an objection to the admission of a document that I have not requested admitted. Now, if Your Honours would like me to go into the document I'm happy to do so, but I've actually not made any request with this respect and it -- but I mean maybe we should simply use the last three minutes before the break to cover this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you would like to discuss a document, but you're not asking for this document to be tendered. So what's the point? What's the point of presenting a document if the Bench cannot use it afterwards, because if the document is not tendered, there will be questions and answers but no more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- as I said, in the interests of time I was going to pass over this document for the time being and see how much time we have at the end because I'm concerned about the time that is available. Now, as I stated, I will be requesting at the end that all the underlying documents get admitted, but I'm at -- I'm at the hands of the Court. If you would like us to deal with this document, it might be convenient for logistical reasons as it is here. It mainly deals with training and equipment -- equipping of volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, have you -- have you discussed Exhibit number 1913 in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I have mentioned that document whereby I also indicated that it is unsigned and that the date is handwritten on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, do you remember on the top -- off the top of your head where this document come from?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was provided by a sensitive source to the investigator during an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If -- with respect to the issue of arming and equipping and maybe training of volunteers, just in short what does this document show?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Yes? *THE ACCUSED: [Interpretation] We are not interested mainly in the contents of the document until we learn from what confidential source it comes and what it is. I know what their confidential source is but they have to say that here to me and to you, that special source whose name is General Aleksandar Vasiljevic, who I have mentioned several times, drew up these documents subsequently for the needs of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Accused Seselj is telling us that the document was handed over by General Aleksandar Vasiljevic. Can you confirm this? No?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I should like to ask this to be redacted from the transcript. The Prosecution cannot have its sensitive sources revealed, and I'm not confirming whether it is correct or not that the document has been provided by that source, but it is impermissible for the accused to say these sort of things in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Mr. Marcussen. We will have ample time to redact this when necessary. I have just read about this person. Is he a protected witness in this case? Because if he is a protected witness in other cases, I know nothing about this. Perhaps the accused with his connections knows that this document was drafted by this general, and he is telling us that so that the Chamber is not under the impression that it is being manipulated and that documents are being presented without anyone knowing where these documents come from. So if this document stems from a witness whom you are going to call to testify, then there's no problem whatsoever. Then I will redact this part of the transcript. But if that is not the case, then we face a problem, because protected sources in other cases apply to the other cases, but in this case it is an accused who is being tried. So this document is in support of the JCE in the sense that the SRS allegedly helped volunteers. So when the judgement is handed down, this could be a very damning document for the accused. So first question, what is the source of the document? Is the source indicated here or does the source stem from another case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Assuming that -- as far as I'm aware this document does not come from a witness in this case. I am reluctant in public session to discuss what source has provided this information to the Tribunal. I'll be happy to -- to make, for example, a written submission on this issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session in that case. Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I believe we sort of ended up in Exhibit 1913. Could you briefly tell us what this document, according to you, tell us about arming and training of volunteers?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, we cannot discuss this document until we know what it is. What is the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Seselj. During the break the Judges considered the matter of objections, and we realised that because of these objections we are wasting a great deal of time. Of course you're entitled to raise objections, but an objection should be made when the Prosecutor asks for a document to be admitted, and the objection may be accepted if the document is a false document. But if you raise an objection for a document that has indicia of reliability or that is related to what the witness says, then we're just wasting time. Secondly, some of your objections pertain to the contents of the expert's report or to his statement, and that's something that you should do as part of your cross-examination, because if you don't proceed that way, then the Chamber has to rule on each and every one of your objections and has to ask questions in order to obtain additional information. I've just been told that the Prosecutor has used 2 hours and 50 minutes with four hours of Judges' questions on the contents, on the substance, and on the objections and so on and so forth. Of course I'm ready to admit that some objections may be justified, but don't object for the sake of objecting, because what matters is the substance. You know that the final judgement will not deal with the objections but with the substance of the documents. If a document is a forged document, no problem. Say it. It's your duty to say it. But if, according to you, this document is not a forged document or if it's a document that has some relevance, please do not raise an objection just to obstruct the examination-in-chief. You are dealing here with Judges who are familiar with the way trials are conducted in this Tribunal. We might be wasting time. I'm going to give the floor, I don't know what you want to say, but let me just say that we decided to tell you this as -- by way of an introduction, but you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you and your colleagues consider that I'm making objections for the purposes of obstruction, then I can give up making any more objections during the examination-in-chief. I can do that. However, I can consider that it is impossible to discuss this particular document because it's not a document at all. It hasn't got the markings of a document. Now, the Prosecutor can find a piece of paper on the street and way, "Now, let's discuss this." So I think this is quite unacceptable, and that is why I'm objecting to it. Now, if you consider that this can be discussed without knowing what it, in fact, is or who wrote it or published it, there's no name, no stamp, no date, there's something handwritten that appears to be a date, but what are we discussing here? Now, if you consider that this objection of mine is obstruction, then I say straight away I am not going to make any more objections if you say I am now obstructing the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have a look at the document in question. What was the number again, Mr. Marcussen, was it 19 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's still the same document as before but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mr. Seselj, I think we -- the matter is closed. *This document comes from General Vasiljevic. It's settled.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your permission, we don't know if it is a document emanating from General Vasiljevic, and I doubt that it is but we don't know whether it is I don't have any proof to show it is. We don't have any proof to show whose document it is. There is no markings there. It's just a piece of paper. Perhaps somebody picked it up from the waste -- the Prosecutor picked it up from a waste paper basket. You can't have documents presented in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have to redact the name of the general. But Prosecutor, Mr. Prosecutor, there's no signature on this document. You ever not provided any additional information with respect to this document. What can you tell us? Because you see, anyone could have given you this document. This might be a document that came from the Office of the Prosecutor. It might be a document coming from someone who is trying to manipulate you. We need to have some information that would allow us to check the relevance, the probative value of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would suggest that we review this document, we proceed with the analysis of this document, and then later on we'll see whether we can find something out about the provenance of this document. Otherwise, we would have seen this document to no avail. We can't keep wasting time this way. We need to move ahead. So if we start look at this document, let's do it properly. That's my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's examine, let's analyse this document and then we'll see what we should do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... documents in my report just to -- for one paragraph that is mentioned in the document that is on the English translation on page 5, and it's the third paragraph from the top where the issue of arming of volunteers, more specifically SRS volunteers, is being discussed. Now, I would like to add that on page -- starting on page 40 in the second part of the report, I include statements by Mr. Seselj and other officials of the War Staff on arming of the volunteers and they include the same information, meaning that the arming was carried out by JNA, Ministry of the Interior the Republic of Serbia, and Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So is it -- if I can paraphrase that, you're saying that this -- the information in this particular document, or at least the part you are quoting this document for is corroborated by all the information in your report and that's why you have included it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I was going to propose that we go to some of these other documents which illustrate this point unless Your Honours want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I may have misunderstood but I have the following question: Witness, you tell us that at paragraph 2 of page 5 of this document, you say that the weapons were provided by the JNA. That's what I thought I understood.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it's the third paragraph, and if I can read it out. It says: "A large number of people who have joined these formation are armed mostly with small arms from depots of the former JNA." Because the document is from 1993 the JNA ceased to exist in May 1992 and was replaced by the VJ. MUP, which means Ministry of Interior and Serbian Ministry of Defence that were distributed in large numbers to volunteer forces engaged on the fronts in Croatia and BiH and in most cases were not returned. The fact that the link -- or the reference is made to the front in Croatia and BiH allows me to conclude that we're talking about the distribution of weapons in 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. But who distributed these weapons? Who distributed the weapons? That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, from a commonsense points of view, weapons which are stored in depots of the JNA are under military control, so weapons can only be taken from these depots with the formal military authorisation which has been provided by -- by the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So it's not the Serbian Radical Party that distributed the weapon but the army that did it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, but the War Staff acted at least as an intermediate in the distribution of weapons to SRS volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if I may, Your Honour, unless you wanted to explore this with this particular document, the next document -- the next couple of documents cast some light on this particular issue. If Your Honours look at the next document in the binder which is 1804, you will see we have a certificate which bears the stamp of the SRS, and this is a document certifying that a certain person has returned a rifle that was issued to him at Bubanj Potok barracks and that this has been returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, these barracks, Mr. Theunens, do you know who were in control of these barracks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, these barracks the Bubanj Potok, which is part of Belgrade, were part of the barracks of the JNA city command in Belgrade. I have also seen information which indicates that the Ministry of Interior took over control of the barracks, but I have not been able to corroborate that latter information. When I mention Ministry of Interior it's Ministry of the interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the next document is number 666, and this is a request from the War Staff to a Territorial Defence and the Bijeljina area, which says: "We ask you to provide a certain quantity of weapons in accordance with the official establishment of a company for the purposes of ..." and so on and so forth. Mr. Theunens, this a document you have looked at also in this context of arming SRS officers -- volunteers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. And again such documents allow to conclude that mechanisms have been put in place in order to distribute the weapons to SRS volunteers through the SRS War Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if Your Honours would follow with me to the next exhibit which is 1129, 65 ter number 1129, we have here a request for uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, would you explain what this document is, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a request signed for Lieutenant General Ljubomir Domazetovic who was responsible for mobilisation at the Federal Secretariat for People's Defence. So the 3rd administration. It's not signed by him, but it's somebody who has the authority to sign in in his place, to issue 50 camouflage uniforms to a group of volunteers through the Federal Secretariat for People's Defence. And Ljubisa Petkovic is authorised or is the person who is designated to be in charge of these volunteers to collect the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And again, Your Honours, if you would follow with me to -- under the next tab which is 65 ter number 1119, we have a similar type document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you would explain us what level in the hierarchy this document belongs to and what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had a personal comment to make, but I'll do that later. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document, 1119, is a receipt, and it's a standardised form used by the Republic of Serbia Ministry of Interior whereby Ljubisa Petkovic, who is the chief the War Staff, signs for the reception of 780 insignia for berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I think maybe we went out of -- out of sync here I think the next document you're referring to is the next one we're going to get to, which is 1539.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Can I ask you to go back there is another SSNO document to the quartermaster dated on the 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It's very similar to 1129.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I jumped a document. I apologise. 1119, yeah, also deals with the issue of uniforms. This time 52 camouflage uniforms by an organ of the SSNO signed by a Colonel Todorovic to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And -- sorry. This is also referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, then the last document in this section of exhibits which deal with arming and equipping is the document that Mr. Theunens just talked about, sorry, 1539. Mr. Theunens, could you repeat what you said about this document, please? It's a receipt?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, a receipt signed by Ljubisa Petkovic for the reception of 780 insignia for berets from the ministry of interior of the Republic of Serbia, and it's dated the 31st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, at this stage I would like to see the admission of these documents and they will have for the reasons already explained be under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, the Prosecutor and the witness must in this document 1539 where mention is made of the Republic of Serbia. Where does it say that? Where does it say that the receipt is taken for the beret insignia from the Republic of Serbia, which they've just told you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at least in the English translation it says, "Receipt." The title of the document is, "Receipt for Weapons and Ammunition Issued by the Republic of Serbia Ministry of the Interior." Now, I don't master Cyrillic, I'm afraid, but it comes from the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it says at the top that this is for Bijeljina. Perhaps you didn't hear me. It says Bijeljina at the top. Not for the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The document is -- the name as I can see it on the top is to Ljubisa Petkovic who is the recipient, and what the Bijeljina reference is we don't know, but the point simply here is that Ljubisa Petkovic received these insignia from the MUP of Serbia. Maybe to be taken to Bijeljina, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Can the witness shed light on this or?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I know that SRS volunteers were involved in the takeover of Bijeljina. They were led by Mirko Blagojevic, but I have no further information in relation to this particular document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you state once again that this is an inappropriate objection, then the same holds true and I won't make any more, but it says Ljubisa Petrovic. The Prosecutor says Ljubisa Petrovic, and I think the witness said the same, whereas the chief of the War Staff of the Serbian Radical Party is Ljubisa Petkovic with a K. Petrovic and Petkovic are two different surnames.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Maybe there's a little mix-up. This receipt seems to be signed by a Petrovic and not Petkovic. That's not the same person. And it seems that this is received in Bijeljina. These are beret insignias, 780 of them. Maybe this has absolutely nothing to do with the SRS.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Might I be allowed to add, Judge, look at the date. It's July. Bijeljina was liberated in April, and this is July, and we're dealing with insignia on police caps, berets, where the Serb flag has been stylised, and they are police insignias, not military ones or volunteer ones. But if you don't think my objection is appropriate, I'll stop it all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Yes, I heard your objection. But, Mr. Prosecutor, do you maintain your request or do you withdraw it? It seems that this document has nothing to do with the SRS. Furthermore, these are insignias for police berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have this document marked for identification. I think if -- well, dependent on which witnesses we eventually get, we will be able to clarify this. This is a document that have been provided to us by a person who will be able to explain this, and -- but it would be best, I think, only to mark it for identification at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, we need some numbers under seal except for this one. This one will get a MFI given the reservations expressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 65 ter numbers or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do so. And the report also for the -- the report 1913 must also be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. 65 ter number 1913 will be Exhibit number P229. I do apologise 65 ter number 1913 will be MFI 229; 65 ter number 1804, Exhibit number P230. 675 ter number 666 will be Exhibit number P231; 65 ter number 1129 will be Exhibit number P232; 65 ter number 1119 will be Exhibit number P233; and 65 ter number 1539 will be MFI P234 all provisionally under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, let me return to what you said earlier. Here -- here in this case your objection was fully justified and well-grounded. So you wanted to note that there are objections that can be grounded, but I also want to show to you that sometimes you raise objections that deal with things that could be dealt with in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next three documents have been included for the purpose of discussing with the witness payment of volunteers and their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what do you conclude about -- well, basically who were volunteers that were sent out by the SRS? Were they being paid?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Like -- like any other volunteer, SRS volunteers were being paid. We see from the documents that are included in the report that this is done through the -- or with the assistance of the SRS War Staff, which has established relations to that effect with the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia. And excuse me, also the intervention or the cooperation with the ministry for -- the Serbian ministry for relations with Serbs outside Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And were arrangements also made for the payment of family members of the SRS in case a volunteer would get killed, for example, at the front?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. And more specific documents can be found in part 2 of the report, page 58 to 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if you would once again follow with me in the binder. There are just three examples of this kind of documents to illustrate this point. The first one is 65 ter number 1020. This is an announcement from the Serbian Radical Party stating: "We're hereby informing all volunteers that wages for participation in combat operations in Western Slavonia, 5th Corps zone of responsibility will be paid on the 26th, 27th, and 28th of March, 2000, from 1300 to 1700 at the 4th July barracks in Belgrade." And then it explains how family members can also collect these wages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the 4th July Barracks Belgrade, who were at those barracks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these were JNA barracks which were also used for the training and equipment of volunteers. The fact that the payment is done in Belgrade indicates that among the SRS volunteers fighting or participating in the fighting in Western Slavonia must be a significant number of people originating from Belgrade or its -- or its surroundings or at least Serbia, because one wouldn't invite locals from Western Slavonia to travel to Belgrade to collect their money.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if Your Honours will follow me then to the next document. It is 639. We have here a document which is relevant to the issue of the financial compensation to family members of killed volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, is this one of the documents you referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and it's of interest that the request is addressed to the ministry for relations with Serbs outside Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, this was sort of a landmark document in the sense that we have now finished binder 1, and I would ask you if you would follow me now to binder 2 to look at the first document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. With this last document -- of course during cross-examination Mr. Seselj can come back to this, but I'm in control of the examination-in-chief; and we want to avoid wasting time, so if we could solve a problem -- or settle a problem right away, it's best to do it immediately rather than wait for the cross-examination. I think that would save time. This document is sent by the Serbian Radical Party to the ministry for relations with Serbs outside Serbia. I'm speaking under your control, Witness, because you have worked on this document. This document states that the Serbian -- obviously the Serbian Radical Party is requesting the approval of the amount of 50.000 dinars being for Aleksandar Mirovic killed in Vukovar on 2nd November 1991; Mirovic being a volunteer who had been assigned to the Vukovar Territorial Defence and who lived in Belgrade, and we have his address. So when I read this document, the Serbian Radical Party is calling on governmental authority, making a request. It's not we pay, it's we request here. So they're asking for 50.000 dinars to be paid out, but who is paying? Is it the Serbian Radical Party, or is it the authority, the governmental authority, who receives this letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ministry for relations with Serbs outside Serbia who makes the payment, and this is in line with -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Serbian Radical Party is drawing the attention of this ministry, requesting for Mirovic's family to be paid out 50.000 dinars, but it's not the Serbian Radical Party that's paying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. What we can conclude from the document is there must be a procedure whereby the Radical Party or the War Staff intervenes on behalf of its volunteers in order to ensure that they are paid or that their relatives are paid in case of the volunteer being killed during the fighting; and it's coherent with what I discussed on page 79 in part 1 of the report where a number of financial measures are being discussed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understood that. But what difference do you make in the fact that, you know, a political party would ask a ministry to pay some kind of amount to a combatant and a social worker that would maybe draw the attention of this ministry on the desperate situation and the destitute situation of this family is or the imam or the Pope or the priest that would send a letter to the ministry drawing the attention of the ministry on the situation of this family, saying 50.000 dinars would come in very handy. Is there a difference that it is a political party asking for the money rather than someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you look at the document in isolation, and if you make abstraction from the fact that the payment is related to the participation in combat operations of this volunteer, there's nothing wrong. Any political party or anyone -- anyone could ask a ministry to provide social for humanitarian assistance to private persons, but what is important is that, first of all, it deals with the payment of a volunteer who is originating from Serbia and who allegedly, according to the document, served in the Vukovar Territorial Defence. So the local Serb Territorial Defence in Vukovar, even though he lived in Belgrade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well, but in the zone of responsibility of the 5th Corps, but that is exactly what is stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure I see this reference, Your Honours, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I was maybe mistaken. There was a previous document where there was a reference to this. It was the previous document that there was a reference to 5th Corps. So here it is a member of the Vukovar Territorial Defence. That's obvious from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. The Vukovar TO, at that time, and we're talking about November 1991, was it part of the armed forces? And I'm not saying JNA. I'm saying armed forces of -- of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as we have discussed earlier, at that moment in time the TO of Vukovar, which prior to the war was part of the TO of the Republic of Croatia, has split, and -- into mono-ethnic or -- let's call it Serb-dominated and Croatian-dominated structures. The Croats have joined the ZNG and forces of the Ministry of Interior, whereas the Serbs continue to call their structure the TO, actually it's the local Serb TO, and they respond to Serbia. They have nothing to do with the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't want to testify for -- on behalf the witness, but just for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But for -- to clarify, Judge Lattanzi asked about the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia. I believe you testified that doesn't exist. What armed forces is it you're answer relate to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, armed forces of the republic that were still existing at the time. It was the Socialist Federative Republic of Serbia. This is the entity I was mentioning. I know -- this was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I just want to make sure there was no conclusion so obviously not. So I don't think we need to go into this further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In very simple terms we could call it forces fighting on the Serbian side, but it would be a highly unscientific definition; but I think we understand each other. Yes, Your Honours, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, before we jump out of this binder could I call you back to 65 ter number 1020, the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, that is the announcement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It's coming up on the screen right now. My question is if you have any information about how the Serbian Radical Party was able to announce and indeed to pay the money that was promised or announced to the volunteers. In other words, is there an underlying document that shows that the SRS was applying for money to pay the volunteers from the government, or do you know if the radical -- the Serbian Radical Party was able to drum up this money from private funds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, to -- to answer in relation to this specific document, my understanding is that the SRS is only making the announcement and inviting its volunteers to come and collect the money at that location, but the money's provided by the Serbian government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you have any evidence of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only evidence of that is the information I discussed in part 1 of the report where I elaborate on the measures taken by the Serbian ministry for Serbs outside of Serbia who announce in the parliament that they have prepared a number of -- taken a number of measures to ensure the financial compensation of payment of volunteers. I have seen documentation about the -- indicated the SRS had obtained financial support from Serbs outside of Serbia donations of humanitarian aid and so on, but I have no information as to whether this -- those donations were used to pay volunteers or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This -- this document is astonishing, if I could say so, because it all depends on how you read it. You will know, for all documents, it all depends how you read it. You could read it with this in mind, thinking that the Serbian Radical Party is paying, which is why my fellow Judge asked the question, and you could not answer it because you say that according to you, it's the government who paid. But -- and if it was the radical, the Serbian Radical Party that was paying, that would be rather astonishing. How could he pay soldiers who were regularly under the 5th Corps of responsibility? Maybe that could be envisaged but that could be quite extraordinary. But secondly if that was the case, then the Serbian Radical Party would need to have very deep pockets to do that, either because through donations or because they had, you know, coffers that were full. That's one way you could read it. And this could be -- this could be detrimental. Now, in the English version, I don't know how this was translated, but when you read the English version it looks like the Serbian Radical Party is making an announcement maybe for political reasons to inform the people that all those who took part in combat operations in Western Slavonia in the 5th Corps zone of responsibility will be paid on March 26, 27, and 28 from 1.00 to 5.00 p.m. in the Belgrade barracks. Then this is a -- might be a political announcement but who is paying, it's the Serbia army -- the Serbian government. So there are two ways to interpret this. How do you interpret this? I'm sure you have drawn conclusion from this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours I think the answer can -- the answer is given in 65 ter number 988, but I don't know whether it's included in the binder; but it's quoted in the statement section in my report on page 58 of part 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Maybe we could call it up in e-court. I don't think we have included this in the binder.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, we won't be wasting time because we're waiting for the Prosecutor. Bubanj Potok barracks is a JNA barracks, and the JNA was on the federal budget, not on the budget of Serbia. This witness ought to know that. He is misleading you intentionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rest assured, Mr. Seselj, nobody can be misleading us. As you have seen, we have just spent five hours putting questions. That is the precise reason why, because we want to avoid making mistakes. So we go to the heart of the matter. So this document, 588, if I'm not mistaken, it's a document 988. It's the one which is on the screen. What does this document say according to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I think it's quite straightforward. It's a letter signed by Ljubisa Petkovic, chief of the SRS War Staff to the ministry. It's translated ministry for liaison with the Serbs, but it's actually the ministry for the relations with the Serbs outside of Serbia wherein Petkovic asks the ministry to stop making payments to volunteers unless they have evidence of their service, i.e., that they can present a certificate; and we have discussed some certificates already earlier during my testimony it. Petkovic adds the second sentence this is especially the case with volunteers sent to war-stricken areas where the Serbian Radical Party. So this brings me back to my earlier reply, that is that the War Staff acts as an intermediate. They keep records of the activities of their volunteers when they started with their service in the war zone, when this service ended, where they served, and so on and so on. They issue certificates to that effect. And that information is then used in order to allow the ministry for relations with Serbs outside of Serbia, of the government of the Republic of Serbia, to make these payments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, but this is what you can read into the document, but one can read into it different things. I discover here that there is a ministry in charge of relations with the Serbs outside Serbia. This ministry which was established, I don't know, under what conditions. Maybe this will be established by documents. This ministry undoubtedly has a budget, without doubt, because at the time the -- this operated on the basis of financial resources. So this document can be interpreted as follows: On the 20th of February, 1992, the SRS informs this ministry that once it pays out the money that it should check that the people who are going to receive the payments are in effect volunteers who have been sent outside. This is something -- this is the way we can look at this document and interpret it. What do you think of this? And this political party which, if they have MPs who are sitting in parliament, have attended the session when the budget was approved. So the idea here is to draw the attention of the ministry so that they do not pay out money to people who do not deserve it. So what do you think of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... listening to you, I understood that you said that the payments are made by the ministry for relations with Serbs outside of Serbia, or maybe I misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that could be one way of looking at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... from the document so that just to summarise, it's the ministry who pays the volunteers based on the information provided by the SRS War Staff. Information consisting of certificates or other records that prove the service of the volunteer. And it implies a recognition by the ministry of the SRS War Staff as being a body that is entitled to carry out these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, maybe it would assist if you would remind us when we discuss the legal framework, I believe you discussed what under the law were the provisions for the payment of volunteers and their status.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you recapsulate that for us just briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. As we discussed initially, and it's also on page 79, page 1 of the report, volunteers were considered equal to conscripts, which means that they have the same benefits, they ever the same duties, but they have the same benefits as conscripts; and in addition to that, on page 79, I discuss a document 65 ter number 7150, which is a reply by the Serbian government to a question posed by a deputy in the Serbian parliament on the measures the government of the Republic of Serbia is intended to take to preserve the welfare of JNA reservists and volunteers from Serbia who are deployed at the front. This response dates from the 5th of December, 1991. And in response an overview of the financial measures is provided. There's talk of personal and family disability allowances, tax reductions for private entrepreneurs,; but that is under consideration. Reduction or exemption of electricity bills. So there is an organised effort on the side of the government of the Republic of Serbia to pay Serbian volunteers who are participating in the conflict in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps we can now move on to the second binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm glad that we managed to move to another binder today, Your Honours. The first document in the next binder is a similar kind of document. It is a certificate issued --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I was just going show this one document, which is also relevant the same issue, and then I was going to ask for the admission of the documents, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this certificate, have you also referred to this in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I've simply included this document so that you have this -- a number of these documents for you to -- to review later on. I don't really wanted to go into detail about this document. It's a certificate issued by the War Staff to a person, to family members of a killed volunteer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you allow me, here the certificate does not indicate the origin of the sum.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I will request the admission under seal then of 1020, 639, 738, and as we also discussed 988 and reviewed that in e-court, I would also request the admission of that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 1020 will be Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to the admission of this document, documents under seal. I demand that these documents be public. There is no reason for them to be confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have told us that, and we have told you that we would rule on this question at the end. So don't say the same thing all over again. You want it to be public, and we have told you that we would rule on that. Registrar, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 1020 will be Exhibit number P235; 65 ter number 639 will be P236; 65 ter number 738 will be Exhibit number 237; and 65 ter number 988 will be Exhibit number P238, all under seal provisionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, we have five hours [as interpreted] before we finish. We can't extend our time for the sake of the interpreters. You've only got five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it would be over optimistic to hope that we can get through the entire subject I'm now going to go through, but I think we should start. Your Honours, what I wanted to discuss next is the requests for assistance sent to the SRS, and so we're now in the second binder and the first document I was going to ask the witness about is 65 ter number 737. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, have you referred to this document in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And for what -- what does this show about the manner in which volunteers were sent out?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document has been discussed in the context of a request by units of the local Serb TO in Western Slavonia where they request the SRS War Staff to provide manpower. Now, this request is also addressed to the Serbian ministry for Serbs outside of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, as these documents are discussed in the report, I was going to go through them quite quickly. The next document is 790, and again this is a request for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, is this also a document you referred to in your report, and what region does relate to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. I've referred to this in my report. It -- first of all, it discusses the situation, military or operational situation in the area of Okucani and Western Slavonia on the 11th and 12th of December. It also talks about enemy activity. And then at the end there is a reference to a ministry to provide -- or to fulfil a request for and then the text is illegible, certain resources that was certainty several days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you -- you said a ministry. Am I correct the document says we expect your speedy and urgent assistance in troops, and we ask the Ministry of Defence in Serbia to approve clothe, footwear, weapons, ammunition and then --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I had overseen that sentence. So the reference to ministry is actually explained two lines above. The Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the next document 1174.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, is this another example you use in your reports to illustrate requests from local TOs to the War Staff for the provision of men and -- and -- and weapons? These two things are mentioned, I think.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed your -- Your Honours this addresses then the situation Odzak and Derventa, which is in northern Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And again, Your Honours, rushing a bit through these documents, they're discussing -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's very good. Just one small question that comes to mind. This request, which is intended to for the defence of this village, this request is addressed to the Serbian Radical Party. Is this request addressed to the Serbian Radical Party, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, because it's -- it's mentioned in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The top left of the document, I mean, the addressees under the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Have you checked whether these Crisis Staffs in this locality did not also send this type of request to other parties? Did they not do this and to send their request to all and other political parties and not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... carried out research to find out also whether actually volunteers were sent, so whether this request was fulfilled, but I have not come across such documents. They may have exist but we don't have them. But at least it shows that the members of the Crisis Staff believe that the SRS War Staff is in a position to assist them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So maybe it would be better to ask for the tendering of documents now and resume tomorrow. It's as you like, Mr. Marcussen. You can ask for the exhibit numbers right now or you may have forgotten in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Nope, you are right, Your Honour, I might have forgotten tomorrow so it is probably a prudent thing to ask for the admission of the documents we have just discussed with the witness; so again I ask under seal, and I think we have noted the accused's objection on this but request under seal the admission of 65 ter numbers 733, 790, and 1174. Oh --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Excuse me. It should have been -- it should not have been 733, it should have been 737.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj has raised a general objection. This has been recorded on the transcript. Registrar, can we have some numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 737 will be Exhibit number P239; 65 ter number 790 will be Exhibit number 240; and 65 ter number 1174 will be Exhibit number P241, all provisionally under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. As you know, we shall begin tomorrow at 9.00. It is usually at 8.30 that we start but anyway, since nobody else is in the courtroom, we can start tomorrow at 9.00. I hope that the examination-in-chief will be concluded tomorrow. We shall try to make sure that we hold our tongues and don't ask too many questions, because I think you have approximately two hours left, and then we might be able to begin with the cross-examination. The cross-examination will also take place during the rest of the week. So anyway, we shall meet again tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.34 p.m.,
